facts_found: Insufficient available balance is the most common decline reason (Code 51); authorization holds, pending debits and scheduled payments reduce available balance before they post, and POS overdraft coverage requires customer opt-in (overdraft_pos_enabled). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

If the balance is genuinely insufficient, the customer should add funds, transfer from another account, or make a smaller transaction and retry. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Code 52 (No Checking Account) means the PIN was accepted but the linked checking account has issues; if the account is actually OPEN it may be a synchronization issue — wait 10-15 minutes and retry. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Code 05 (Do Not Honor) is a catch-all requiring investigation in this order: card status (FROZEN/CLOSED/PENDING/ACTIVE), linked account status, fraud_alert_active with alert_source, then velocity_blocked. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

If the linked account status is SUSPENDED or RESTRICTED, the customer must visit a branch or call 1-800-RHO-ACCT; specific details must not be disclosed. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

A bank-initiated fraud alert cannot be cleared by customer service; the customer is transferred to the security team. A customer-initiated alert can be cleared after identity verification and confirmation that recent transactions are legitimate. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

A velocity block temporarily blocks the card due to unusual activity patterns; it automatically lifts after 30 minutes and can be cleared earlier by an agent after identity verification. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Codes 55 (Incorrect PIN) and 75 (PIN Tries Exceeded) indicate PIN problems; if pin_locked is TRUE the PIN Lock Investigation Protocol fraud risk scoring must be completed before any unlock. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_010]

Code 83 (Unable to Verify PIN) is a network problem, not a wrong PIN: retry the transaction, then try a signature-based transaction, a different terminal or merchant, and if persistent wait 10-15 minutes. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_010]

Code 54 means the card is expired; Code 14 means an invalid/old card number was used; Code 56 means no card record exists (verify it is actually a Rho-Bank card). [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

Code 61 means the transaction exceeds the card's daily purchase or ATM limit; remaining capacity is daily limit minus amount already used today, and temporary limit increases last 24 hours. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

Code 65 (Activity Count Exceeded) means too many transactions in the period; count limits are typically fixed and reset at midnight, so the customer must wait or use a different card. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

Code 57 indicates cardholder restrictions (restricted MCCs, international_enabled FALSE, online_enabled FALSE, or parental controls); Code 62 indicates geographic restrictions or a new card still inside its 24-hour post-activation security hold. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

Code 58 means the specific merchant terminal is flagged; neither the customer nor agent can resolve it — try a different register at the same store or a different merchant. Repeated declines at multiple unrelated terminals point to a card issue and require Code 05 diagnostics. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

Codes 19, 91, 96 and 92 are transient system/network/routing issues: retry immediately (Code 19), otherwise wait 10-15 minutes, try a different merchant or payment method, or use an ATM which routes differently. [doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_009]

Code 82 (chip/CVV mismatch) suggests a damaged chip or magnetic stripe — order a replacement; if the card looks undamaged it may indicate a cloned card and recent transactions must be reviewed. [doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_007]
Code 87 means the decline was caused by a cash-back request that is not permitted; retry the purchase without cash back. [doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_007]

Codes 41 (lost card) and 43 (stolen card) mean the card was previously reported; lost and stolen cards cannot be reactivated and require a replacement, and Code 43 requires enhanced verification. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Codes 04, 07, 34 and 59 are internal-only suspected-fraud/capture codes that must never be disclosed to the customer; the customer is told there is a security matter requiring in-person branch verification, and transfer_to_human_agents is used if they press for details. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

A frozen card declines all new transactions and recurring payments; the customer can unfreeze at any time through the mobile app or by calling customer service, and unfreezing takes effect immediately. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

If pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' the card cannot be unlocked by chat agents and the customer must be offered a transfer to the security team; risk scores of 11-14 cannot be unlocked on the call, and 15+ cannot be unlocked at all (recommend closure and replacement). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_041]

Escalate to the security team when a fraud alert is bank-initiated, the customer cannot verify identity, the customer reports transactions they did not make, the caller may not be the account holder, or the explanation for unusual activity is suspicious or inconsistent. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Declined POS attempts are recorded as transactions of type 'pos_declined' (and 'atm_withdrawal_declined'), which agents review when diagnosing card problems. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_041]
Customers receive a declined-transaction notification according to their alert settings, and can retry after adding funds. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_006]

On no-overdraft accounts such as the Green Account, purchases are authorized only up to the available balance and any charge above it is declined immediately with no overdraft. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_003]

Transfer reason codes are tiered; 'fraud_or_security_concern' (Tier 1) covers fraud, identity theft, unauthorized transactions and security concerns, and 'technical_system_error' (Tier 1) covers a system error or outage preventing completion of the request. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

facts_found: get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 is the internal tool that retrieves a customer's bank accounts (checkings and savings); it requires the customer's user_id and returns account_id, account_type, account_class, status, balance and date_opened. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823(account_id) looks up all debit cards associated with a specific checking account; account_id is the checking account ID. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

The debit card lookup returns card_id, account_id, user_id, card_number_last_4, status (ACTIVE, PENDING, FROZEN, CLOSED), issue_reason, expiration_date (MM/YY), date_issued, card_design, daily_purchase_limit and daily_atm_limit. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

The debit card lookup only returns cards for checking accounts (savings accounts have no debit cards), may return multiple cards including old closed ones, never returns full card numbers (last 4 only), and returns an empty list if no cards exist. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

get_bank_account_transactions_9173(account_id) retrieves the transaction history for a checking or savings account and returns transactions in reverse chronological order (most recent first). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

Each transaction record contains transaction_id, account_id, date (MM/DD/YYYY), description, amount (positive = credit, negative = debit), type and status ('posted' or 'pending'). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

Declined card attempts are reviewed as transactions of type 'atm_withdrawal_declined' or 'pos_declined' when performing the debit-card fraud-risk assessment, and the declined transaction's description carries the merchant city used for location scoring. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_041]

The Code 05 diagnostic explicitly reads card status, fraud_alert_active, alert_source and velocity_blocked 'from the debit card lookup response', and account status from the account lookup — confirming steps 1-2 supply the card/account diagnostics. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

Code 51 diagnosis uses the checking balance from the account lookup plus pending transactions from the transaction history and the account's overdraft_pos_enabled field. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_006]

Codes 57/61/62/65 diagnosis uses fields read from the debit card lookup: restricted_mccs, international_enabled, online_enabled, allowed_regions/blocked_regions, date_issued, daily_purchase_limit/daily_atm_limit, daily_purchase_used/daily_atm_used, daily_transaction_count/daily_transaction_limit. [doc_checking_accounts_light_green_account_005]

Codes 55/75 diagnosis uses the card's pin_locked and pin_attempts_remaining fields from the debit card lookup; if pin_locked is TRUE the PIN Lock Investigation Protocol (fraud risk scoring) must be completed before any unlock. [doc_checking_accounts_green_account_(checking)_010]

clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892(card_id, reason) clears customer-initiated fraud alerts or velocity blocks; reason must be 'customer_verified' or 'velocity_clear', and it cannot clear bank-initiated alerts (transfer to security team instead). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

The transaction-type enum published for get_bank_account_transactions_9173 lists debit_card_purchase, atm_withdrawal, direct_deposit, ach/wire types, check/mobile deposit, bill_pay, everyonepay, monthly_fee, overdraft_fee, fee_rebate, interest_credit, rebate_credit, fee_refund — it does not itself list 'pos_declined', which appears in the PIN-lock protocol's description of declined transaction history. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

No knowledge-base article documents a dedicated tool or response field that returns the numeric decline code for a specific declined POS attempt; the decline-code articles assume the code is already known from the customer/merchant and then tell the agent which lookup fields to inspect. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

open_questions: No documented tool or response field that returns the numeric decline_code for a specific declined POS attempt; the code must be obtained from the customer/merchant receipt or the customer's declined-transaction alert, then interpreted against the decline-code articles.

get_bank_account_transactions_9173 is documented as taking only account_id — no date range, transaction-type filter, or card_id parameter is documented, so 'recent' declines must be identified by scanning the reverse-chronological result set.

The published transaction 'type' enum for get_bank_account_transactions_9173 omits 'pos_declined'/'atm_withdrawal_declined', which the PIN-lock protocol says agents review; the authoritative field list for declined attempts is therefore slightly inconsistent.
Sarah Chen's actual user_id, checking account_id(s), card_id(s) and account tier/card type are not in the knowledge base and must come from the live tool calls.

Whether the debit card lookup response includes timestamp granularity for declined attempts (needed for the B1/B3 time-of-day and attempt-velocity scoring) is not documented; the transaction record only documents a date field.

Code 43 requires ENHANCED verification: full name, date of birth, AND last 4 of SSN, AND recent transaction verification (ask about 2-3 recent transactions). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

After enhanced verification the agent may say: 'This card was reported stolen. For security, stolen cards cannot be reactivated. I can order you a replacement card with a new number.' [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

If the customer insists they never reported the card stolen, that is a MAJOR security flag (someone may have access to their account); the agent must say 'For your protection, I need to transfer you to our security team who can investigate this further,' use transfer_to_human_agents, and must NOT attempt to resolve it themselves. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Code 41 (Lost Card) analog: if the customer says they did not report it, treat as a SECURITY CONCERN that someone else may have reported it, ask security questions, note that verification may indicate account compromise, and review recent transaction history for suspicious activity. Codes 04, 07, 34 and 59 are internal-use-only: do not tell the customer the specific code or reason; for Codes 34/59 say 'There's a security matter affecting your card that requires in-person verification. verified_facts: For a suspected in-store fraudulent use of the physical card, dispute with dispute_category 'card_present_fraud', which maps to card_action 'close_and_reissue'; the agent must still separately perform the card action after filing. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_031]

Dispute pre-filing requirements: customer verified, transaction at least $1.00, within 60 days old, under the account tier's open-dispute cap (Entry 2 / Mid 3 / Premium 4 / Elite 5), and the debit card must be linked to an OPEN checking account. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_031]

Before filing, inform the customer of Regulation E liability exposure: within 2 business days max $50; within 60 days max $500; after 60 days unlimited. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_031]

The dispute workflow requires asking 'Do you still have your physical debit card in your possession?' (card_in_possession) and 'Do you believe your PIN may have been compromised?' (pin_compromised). [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_031]

Closing a debit card for 'lost', 'stolen' or 'fraud_suspected' bypasses the 14-day minimum card age requirement; the agent must inform the customer that pending transactions will still process, ask whether they want a replacement immediately, and advise reviewing recent transactions and filing disputes for unauthorized charges. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

Close eligibility requires the card be in ACTIVE or PENDING status with no pending transactions or pending refunds; closed cards cannot be reopened and refunds to a closed card credit the linked checking account. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

After a fraud_suspected closure, recommend the customer also change their online banking password; lost/stolen cards are closed immediately with no cooling-off period. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

Freeze is a temporary lock (card must be ACTIVE to freeze; all new and recurring transactions decline while frozen); if the customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

Replacement cards issued for lost/stolen/fraud must be activated with activate_debit_card_8292, after which the agent must remind the customer to review recent transactions, ask about suspicious activity, and recommend changing the online banking password if fraud was suspected. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_024]

Lost/stolen cross-product protocol: after the debit card freeze/close procedure, check for Rho-Bank credit cards with get_credit_card_accounts_by_user and proactively offer a replacement credit card with a new number; if declined, note in the account that the offer was made. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030]

Code 05 step 3: if fraud_alert_active is TRUE and alert_source is 'bank_initiated', do NOT clear it — say 'I see there's a security flag on your account that requires additional review. I'm transferring you to our security team' and transfer to human agents. [source: doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

Code 05 step 2: if the linked account status is not OPEN, do not provide specific details for SUSPENDED or RESTRICTED status; direct the customer to a branch or 1-800-RHO-ACCT. [source: doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

transfer_to_human_agents reason 'fraud_or_security_concern' (Tier 1) is used for fraud, identity theft, unauthorized transactions, or security concerns requiring specialist handling; always select from the highest applicable tier. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Debit card ordering options are STANDARD (free, 7-10 business days), EXPEDITED ($15, 3-5 business days) and RUSH ($35, 1-2 business days), with fees possibly varying by account tier; a customer cannot have more than 1 active debit card per checking account. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_023]

The KB has no article keyed to alert_source 'stolen_report' or stolen_reported_by 'unknown_caller'; the only documented alert sources are 'customer_initiated' and 'bank_initiated', so a report placed by an unknown caller is handled as a non-customer (security-sensitive) report requiring escalation. [source: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]
open_questions: Sarah Chen's actual user_id, checking account_id(s), card_id(s) and account tier/card type are not in the knowledge base and must come from the live tool calls.

Whether the debit card lookup response includes timestamp granularity for declined attempts (needed for the B1/B3 time-of-day and attempt-velocity scoring) is not documented; the transaction record only documents a date field.

The KB defines alert_source only as 'customer_initiated' or 'bank_initiated'; there is no article mapping the observed values 'stolen_report' / stolen_reported_by 'unknown_caller' to one of those categories, so whether the 4738 alert is technically clearable must be inferred (non-customer-placed = not clearable) or confirmed by attempting the clear call and reading the error.

No KB article describes a vishing/social-engineering or 'third party filed a report on the customer's behalf' playbook beyond the Code 41/43 'customer says they did not report it' branch.

Whether the transfer to the security team must be merely offered versus executed without customer consent is stated as mandatory only for the Code 43 denial branch and bank-initiated alerts; for the cloned-card/velocity path the language is 'offer to transfer'.
The customer's checking account tier is unknown, so the open-dispute cap (Entry 2 / Mid 3 / Premium 4 / Elite 5) and any tier-based replacement shipping fee waivers cannot be applied.

No documented tool returns the decline code for the 5847 chip failures, and no 'pos_declined' records exist in the three accounts' histories, so the PIN Lock fraud risk score cannot be computed from declined-transaction data.
